"executive_summary": "This paper establishes a fundamental equivalence between the systems of Hecke eigenvalues appearing in the coherent cohomology of compact Shimura varieties and those appearing in any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme, including singular or higher-dimensional ones. The author, Stefan Reppen, generalizes previous results by Goldring-Koskivirta and Terakado-Yu, which were restricted to smooth, zero-dimensional subschemes like Ekedahl-Oort strata. The core innovation involves a novel 'further going-down argument' that constructs a smooth, closed subscheme ZK from an arbitrary subscheme YK by intersecting with the smallest length stratum and removing nonsingular points. This construction allows the use of Hasse invariants to bridge the gap between the cohomology of the singular subscheme and the smooth auxiliary subscheme. The paper proves that the Hecke eigenvalues on the original subscheme YK are identical to those on the Shimura variety SK, provided SK is of abelian type at hyperspecial level. The results extend to noncompact Shimura varieties and nonclosed subschemes, such as central leaves, under specific conditions regarding the basic locus or the existence of nowhere vanishing sections. The work relies heavily on the theory of G-zips, the structure of Ekedahl-Oort and length stratifications, and the properties of automorphic line bundles on the special fiber of integral models.",

summary.title: Systems of Hecke Eigenvalues on Subschemes of Shimura Varieties
summary.executive_summary: This paper establishes a fundamental equivalence between the systems of Hecke eigenvalues appearing in the coherent cohomology of compact Shimura varieties and those appearing in any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme, including singular or higher-dimensional ones. The author, Stefan Reppen, generalizes previous results by Goldring-Koskivirta and Terakado-Yu, which were restricted to smooth, zero-dimensional subschemes like Ekedahl-Oort strata. The core innovation involves a novel 'further going-down argument' that constructs a smooth, closed subscheme ZK from an arbitrary subscheme YK by intersecting with the smallest length stratum and removing nonsingular points. This construction allows the use of Hasse invariants to bridge the gap between the cohomology of the singular subscheme and the smooth auxiliary subscheme. The paper proves that the Hecke eigenvalues on the original subscheme YK are identical to those on the Shimura variety SK, provided SK is of abelian type at hyperspecial level. The results extend to noncompact Shimura varieties and nonclosed subschemes, such as central leaves, under specific conditions regarding the basic locus or the existence of nowhere vanishing sections. The work relies heavily on the theory of G-zips, the structure of Ekedahl-Oort and length stratifications, and the properties of automorphic line bundles on the special fiber of integral models.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper establishes a fundamental equivalence between the systems of Hecke eigenvalues appearing in the coherent cohomology of compact Shimura varieties and those appearing in any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme, including singular or higher-dimensional ones. The author, Stefan Reppen, generalizes previous results by Goldring-Koskivirta and Terakado-Yu, which were restricted to smooth, zero-dimensional subschemes like Ekedahl-Oort strata. The core innovation involves a novel 'further going-down argument' that constructs a smooth, closed subscheme ZK from an arbitrary subscheme YK by intersecting with the smallest length stratum and removing nonsingular points. This construction allows the use of Hasse invariants to bridge the gap between the cohomology of the singular subscheme and the smooth auxiliary subscheme. The paper proves that the Hecke eigenvalues on the original subscheme YK are identical to those on the Shimura variety SK, provided SK is of abelian type at hyperspecial level. The results extend to noncompact Shimura varieties and nonclosed subschemes, such as central leaves, under specific conditions regarding the basic locus or the existence of nowhere vanishing sections. The work relies heavily on the theory of G-zips, the structure of Ekedahl-Oort and length stratifications, and the properties of automorphic line bundles on the special fiber of integral models.

Research Context
Shimura varieties at mod p fibers possess Hecke actions on their cohomology. Subschemes like Ekedahl-Oort strata are invariant under this Hecke action. Prior work related eigenvalues on the variety to those on zero-dimensional strata. Goldring-Koskivirta proved equality for zero-dimensional Ekedahl-Oort strata. Terakado-Yu extended this to zero-dimensional central leaves in the basic stratum. Existing proofs rely on subschemes being smooth of dimension zero. Higher dimensional and singular subschemes present new challenges.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The paper asks if eigenvalue systems match for higher dimensional subschemes. The hypothesis is that eigenvalues on any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme match the variety. The author predicts this holds for Ekedahl-Oort strata and length strata. The author predicts this holds for central leaves under properness conditions. The predicted outcome is equality of the systems of Hecke eigenvalues. The method must overcome the lack of nowhere vanishing sections on singular schemes. The method must overcome the failure of the conormal sequence to be exact.

Methodological Details
The study uses the special fiber of the Kisin-Vasiu integral canonical model. The level is assumed to be hyperspecial for the prime-to-p Hecke algebra. The group G is assumed to be the cuspidal quotient Gc. The prime p is fixed such that G is unramified over it. The theory relies on the stack of G-zips of type µ. Automorphic vector bundles are defined via pullback from G-zips. The Ekedahl-Oort stratification is induced by the map to G-zips. Hasse invariants exist for each Ekedahl-Oort stratum and length stratum. Central leaves are defined via isomorphism of Dieudonné modules. The Hecke action is defined via push-pull operators on cohomology. The proof constructs a smooth subscheme ZK from YK by intersecting with strata. Nonsingular points are removed iteratively to ensure smoothness. The resulting ZK admits a nowhere vanishing Hecke-equivariant section. The argument uses the conormal exact sequence modified for the ideal sheaf. Serre vanishing is used to ensure the vanishing of higher cohomology groups.

Procedures And Architectures
The model used is the integral canonical model of the Shimura variety. The automorphic line bundles V(η) correspond to L-dominant characters. The cohomology modules are direct sums over dominant characters. The proof of Theorem A proceeds by induction on the length stratification. The subscheme ZK is defined as the minimal stable subscheme in the chain. The Hasse invariant Hai0 restricts to a nowhere vanishing section on ZK. The injectivity of the section h is established using Lemma 2.5.1. Lemma 3.2.2 relates eigenvalues on YK to those on the smooth ZK. Lemma 3.2.4 relates eigenvalues on ZK to those on the full variety SK. For noncompact cases, a toroidal compactification SΣK is utilized. The Hecke action extends to the toroidal compactification. Equality for nonclosed subschemes relies on the basic locus. The proof uses the fact that central leaves in the basic locus are zero-dimensional. The argument for nonclosed subschemes uses restriction to the nonvanishing locus. The extension of eigenforms is guaranteed by Grothendieck's theorem.

Key Results
Theorem A states equality for any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme. Theorem B extends this to Ekedahl-Oort strata and length strata. Theorem B includes central leaves under properness conditions. The systems of eigenvalues are identical for the variety and the subscheme. The result holds for the closure of all subschemes mentioned in the introduction. The result holds for nonclosed subschemes meeting the basic locus. The result holds for subschemes pulled back from closed substacks of G-zips. The result holds for the nonvanishing locus of a Hecke-equivariant section. Corollary 3.3.3 confirms equality for Ekedahl-Oort strata and central leaves. The proof establishes a chain of equivalences through the smooth subscheme ZK. The existence of Hasse invariants is crucial for the going-up argument. The method works for both compact and noncompact Shimura varieties. The result is independent of the specific choice of the subscheme YK. The result holds for any G(Ap f)-equivariant system of closed subschemes.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The result implies that Hecke eigenvalues are robust across different subscheme types. It generalizes Serre's letter to Tate regarding modular curves. It extends Goldring-Koskivirta's theorem to higher dimensions. It extends Terakado-Yu's theorem to non-zero-dimensional central leaves. The smooth subscheme ZK acts as a bridge between singular and smooth theories. The result suggests a deep connection between the geometry of strata and Hecke modules. The method provides a unified framework for studying eigenvalues on various subschemes. It confirms that the Hasse invariant is the key tool for relating eigenvalues. The result applies to the integral canonical model, not just the smooth locus. It implies that the cohomology of the variety is determined by its strata.

Contradictions And Limitations
The assumption G = Gc is technical and restricts the generality. The theory of toroidal compactifications for abelian type is not yet developed. The result for noncompact varieties requires the Hodge type assumption. The result for nonclosed subschemes requires meeting the basic locus. The result for central leaves requires them to be closed in the containing stratum. The result for nonclosed subschemes requires the existence of an ample divisor. The proof relies on the existence of Hasse invariants which may not exist in all contexts. The result is limited to the special fiber at good reduction. The result is limited to prime-to-p Hecke actions. The result is limited to the coherent cohomology with coefficients in automorphic line bundles.

Claims
The systems of Hecke eigenvalues on any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme are identical to those on the Shimura variety. The systems of Hecke eigenvalues that appear in the coherent cohomology... are the same as those appearing in any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme M(YK) ↭H M(ZK) ↭H M(SK) Theorem A applies in particular to the closure of all subschemes mentioned in the first paragraph The theory of toroidal compactifications of abelian type Shimura varieties has not yet been developed If (G, X) is neither of compact-type nor of PEL-type, then assume that there exists a G(Ap f)-equivariant divisor D′ The result generalizes Serre's letter to Tate regarding modular curves The result extends Goldring-Koskivirta's theorem to higher dimensions The result extends Terakado-Yu's theorem to non-zero-dimensional central leaves
The method involves constructing a smooth subscheme ZK from a singular subscheme YK by intersecting with the smallest length stratum. By intersecting YK with the smallest length stratum that it intersects nontrivially and by successively removing the nonsingular points of this intersection we obtain a smooth, closed subscheme ZK ⊂YK One thus faces two problems; (1) there is no nowhere vanishing Hecke-invariant section on YK (2) the conormal sequence is neither exact nor consists of locally free sheaves This construction allows the use of Hasse invariants to bridge the gap between the cohomology of the singular subscheme and the smooth auxiliary subscheme The resulting ZK admits a nowhere vanishing Hecke-equivariant section The proof establishes a chain of equivalences through the smooth subscheme ZK
The result holds for noncompact Shimura varieties and nonclosed subschemes under specific conditions. We also obtain results regarding nonclosed subschemes and noncompact Shimura varieties If YK meets the basic locus, then M(SK) ↭H M(YK) If YK = ζ∗KYK for a closed substack Y of G-Zipµ, then M(YK) ↭H M(SK) As far as we know, the theory of toroidal compactifications of abelian type Shimura varieties has not yet been developed Hence, in this section we assume that if (G, X) is not of compact-type, then it is of Hodge type The result applies to the integral canonical model, not just the smooth locus The result is independent of the specific choice of the subscheme YK The result holds for any G(Ap f)-equivariant system of closed subschemes

Data And Code Availability
The paper is a theoretical mathematical proof with no data or code to share.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The proof relies on the existence of Hasse invariants which may not exist in all contexts. The result is limited to the special fiber at good reduction. The result is limited to prime-to-p Hecke actions. The result is limited to the coherent cohomology with coefficients in automorphic line bundles.

Three Takeaways
The core contribution is the generalization of Hecke eigenvalue equality to higher dimensional and singular subschemes. The strongest evidence is the construction of the smooth subscheme ZK via intersection with the smallest length stratum. The future path involves developing the theory of toroidal compactifications for abelian type Shimura varieties.
